title: Mummies
text: The ancient Egyptians believed in a life after death. They thought that the body was necessary for this new life, so they made mummies to protect it.

Making a mummy took about seventy days. First, the priests removed the organs. They put the stomach, the lungs and other organs in special jars. They left the heart in the body, because the heart was important in the afterlife.

Then they covered the body with a salt called natron. It dried the body completely in about forty days. After that, they wrapped the body in hundreds of meters of linen. Between the layers they put amulets for protection.
Finally, they put the mummy in a coffin, often in the shape of a person, and placed it in a tomb with food, furniture and treasures. They held a big ceremony at sunset.
Not only people became mummies. The Egyptians also mummified cats, birds, crocodiles and even dogs. In the 19th century, archaeologists found millions of animal mummies in a single cemetery!
q: Why did the Egyptians make mummies?
To protect the body for the afterlife
